reader.requirement: At 1985 each symbolic-character-1 must denote, in storage and in every comparison/move/STRING, the native character (the native internal representation) of the character GR8 selects, whether integer-1 is a native ordinal or (IN alphabet-name-2) an ordinal in a STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2/NATIVE/implementor-name/literal alphabet, independent of the program collating sequence.

edition-consulted.switches: refuses the FOR ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL phrase before 2002 (Constructs.SpecialNamesForNational2002); the value computation itself is edition-blind

reader.edition-search: grep CobolVersion|IsAtLeast|DialectBehavior|ConstructRegistry|Edition.Version in SpecialNamesBinder*.cs, CollatingModel.cs, ImplementorCodeNames.cs: only the RANGE IN alphabet gate (unrelated) and currency; SwitchBindSymbolic uses Edition only as a diagnostic sink (Edition.At).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: the value (native char of the selected character) is computed by one edition-blind path; only the 2002 FOR phrase is gated

reader.notes: SwitchBindSymbolic stores the symbolic value as a native .NET character: native ordinal n -> code unit n-1, IN alphabet -> CodedCharacterSet.CharAt, which inverts the alphabet's table to the native character (ALSO: literal-1). Probes over EBCDIC, NATIVE, literal (including unspecified tail behaviour not probed) and STANDARD-1 (witness) all yield the native character.

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4 a-d (with Amendment 2's new d4 and the d6 ALSO sentence), GR8, GR9, SR10 and CodedCharacterSet.CharAt / SwitchBindSymbolic. Probe refute-1985-103/rs1.cob (rs1-001) used a literal alphabet the reader did not try: "Z" ALSO "Y", a descending THRU "B" THRU "A", a native-ordinal literal 69, then "C". It printed LZ=Z LB=B LA=A LD=D LC=C, so ALSO uses literal-1 only (GR4 d6): INSPECT TALLYING FOR ALL LZ on 'ZYZA' gave CNT=02, not 3. The first unspecified ordinal (6) is LOW-VALUE (U+0000), the implementor's d4 determination, which CodedCharacterSet documents. STANDARD-2 ordinals 66/37 gave A/$; NATIVE 35 gave '"'; VALUE LZ and MOVE ALL LB gave Z and BBBB; a contained program sees LA and NQ (GR1). rs2.cob (rs2-001, compile-only) refused the later editions' forms at 85: a constant-name ordinal (the constant entry needs COBOL-2002, COBOL0900) and IN a UTF-8 alphabet (COBOL0900 plus COBOL5986). Greps of SpecialNamesBinder*.cs and CollatingModel.cs for DialectLevel|IsAtLeast|CobolVersion|ConstructRegistry find only the Currency, LOCALE and RANGE gates, none of them on this path. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR9 (the text is in GR9); OK §1985:VI.4.5.4 GR4 ('only literal-1 is used to represent the character in the native character set', the text is in GR4). A reading I did not pursue: the code maps STANDARD-2 ordinal 37 to '$'. That is a GR4a question, whether the 1985 IRV puts the currency sign at 0x24, and not a GR9 question.
